metadata.title: Creating Effective Teaching and Learning Environments: First Results from TALIS – ISBN 978-92-64-05605-3

survey_design.weight_variable_name: TCHWGT (teacher final weights) and TRWGT1–TRWGT100 (BRR replicates)
survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TALIS lower secondary teacher and school principal survey data collected in 2007–08 across 23 participating countries (with the Netherlands excluded from international comparisons due to unmet sampling standards). For the regression analyses described in Annex A1.4, the authors apply complex survey weighting at the teacher level using the “final teacher weight” (TCHWGT) and variance estimation via Balanced Repeated Replication (BRR) with Fay’s adjustment. For Chapter 7 models, teacher final weights (TCHWGT) and 100 BRR replicate weights (TRWGT1–TRWGT100) are used, including in the multiple-imputation workflow. Missing data are handled separately (listwise deletion in earlier chapters; multiple imputation in Chapter 7), but weighting is consistently part of the estimation strategy to reflect the clustered, stratified TALIS sampling design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: not_applicable is used because TALIS in this report models teacher- and school-level indices and self-efficacy/job satisfaction measures rather than cognitive achievement scores with Plausible Values. The dependent variables are survey-based indices (e.g., classroom disciplinary climate, teacher self-efficacy) and do not rely on PV-based scaling. Missing data handling is explicitly described for Chapter 7 via multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption, so the PV/missing-data transparency issue does not apply here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report targets lower secondary education teachers and their school principals, with an international design of 200 schools per country and 20 teachers per school. For the regression analyses in Annex A1.4, regressions are run separately for each country. Chapter 7 includes teacher- and school-level variables drawn from Chapters 2–6, and it imputes missing values for the dependent variables (classroom disciplinary climate index and teacher self-efficacy index) and independent variables to maintain adequate sample size. Earlier chapters (e.g., Chapters 4 and 6) use listwise deletion for missing data. The Netherlands is excluded from international comparisons because it did not meet TALIS sampling requirements; its data are only summarized in Annex A2.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS report (first round implemented in 2007–08) uses complex survey regression analyses to describe associations between teacher/school context variables and two key learning-environment indicators: the classroom disciplinary climate index and teachers’ self-efficacy index. The report does not use machine learning; instead it applies multiple regression and multilevel regression (random intercept models) where appropriate, run separately for each country, with BRR variance estimation and Fay’s adjustment. For missing data, earlier chapters use listwise deletion, while Chapter 7 imputes missing values using multiple imputation (five imputed datasets) under a missing-at-random assumption, then combines estimates across imputations. The analysis is weighted using teacher final weights (TCHWGT) and replicate weights (TRWGT1–TRWGT100) to reflect TALIS’s clustered sampling design. Because the study is cross-sectional and based on self-reports, the reported “effects” are statistical net associations rather than causal impacts.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is limited to the technical annex text provided, which specifies regression procedures, weighting, and missing-data handling but does not include the actual regression results tables (coefficients/effect sizes) for the dependent variables. Therefore, no empirical ML predictive targets or model-performance metrics can be populated into main_findings without fabricating results. The study is still clearly empirical and uses regression modeling, but the provided excerpt does not contain the outcome-specific effect estimates needed for StructuredFinding rows.
